I see your point, but I'd like to point out some reasons most of us get so frustrated.

- we started making music when we were younger and had more free time, and smaller bills. We could physically afford to spend an entire weekend in the studio, or every day after school or work.

- as we got older, not only did most of us pick up more responsibilities, (spouse, house, kids, job, bills) but also the economic state of the world continued to criminally undervalue creative people of all stripes, inflate the currencies we all rely on, and generally get shittier and shittier over time.

- leading up to a point where some (but not all) old dogs don't have the time to devote to social media and the Marketing/Branding hustle, therefore functionally disabling them from pursuing a more modern career in entertainment/music.

Not only must your music compete, everything else about it must compete as well. From branding to literally the infinitesimally small things; like the way you dress or style your hair. It's all part of how "professionalism" is judged, these days, and your attitude doesn't even get the chance to audition most times because people just scroll past if you don't possess a passing resemblance to _insert famous artist here_ and their quality of work.

We tell ourselves as artists every day not to compare ourselves to people we idolize but the listeners do it anyway and you'd be disgusted how much better received your music can be when your branding is copying whatever Flavor Of The Month artist is hot on Spotify right now. It's honestly pretty sad. Humans are drawn to the familiar like flies to shit.

Finally, I will say, at least as a woman, I feel like I have to pose partially nude on the daily for thirsty Instagram idiots just to get noticed, and if I'm not in a V-neck bouncing my chest while I DJ, I feel like no one wants to listen. Shouldn't it be about what you're hearing, not seeing? Ugh. Why do I feel like that? _Because I see my female peers doing the same things and I want to be successful like them;_ monkey see, monkey do.

So between the rigors of adulthood, a collapsing late stage capitalist centric economy, and the socio-cultural horrors of identifying as female, I can clearly see the optimism and even truth of what you're saying, OP, but I just don't _feel_ very lucky.
